title: Value or Fallback
hints: A pointer holds either `nullptr` or the address of an `int`. `*p` reads the int at that address, and that is only legal when `p` is not null. Test the *pointer* (`if (p)`), never the pointee (`if (*p)`), because `*p` is itself a dereference.

The conditional expression does it in one line:
```cpp
return p ? *p : fallback;
```
